newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TO END STATE MONOPOLY ON GRAIN PURCHASES.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TO END STATE MONOPOLY ON GRAIN PURCHASES.

text.p: Romania is restructuring its National Agency for Agricultural Products (ANPA) grain agency to end the state grain monopoly and decentralise the sector, an official publication said on Friday.
Under a bill approved by the government, state-run ANPA would be split into 29 commercial companies headquartered in main crop areas, the Official Gazette said.
Restructuring of ANPA, Romania's main grain purchaser and exporter, would be completed within the next 45 days, it said.

The move to restructure the oversized agency is part of the new centrist government's tough economic reform programme to end a communist-era monopoly on grain purchasing and storage as well as to adjust the farm sector to market economics and introduce competition.
It also lays the ground for smooth harvesting and storage of the expected wheat crop of eight million tonnes in 1997.

Under the bill, the new companies would be allowed to purchase and store grain and store strategic state stocks as well as import and export. They would also offer a wide range of services in the farming sector including credits, transport, land lease and hire of storage facilities.
The government has pledged to support the farming sector, whose contribution to the country's Gross National Product (GDP) amounted to over 20 percent last year.
On Thursday, the Agriculture Ministry said it would add 950 billion lei to initial funds of 450 billion lei earmarked for wheat purchases this year.
Romania became a major force on the world grain market in 1995 when it sold almost 1.5 million tonnes of wheat. REUTER
